steps.title: AVG per supplier_id
steps.prompt:
GROUP BY bundles rows into piles that share the same supplier_id.
Then avg(supplier_id) works on each pile.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT supplier_id, avg(supplier_id) FROM products GROUP BY supplier_id;
hints: Start with SELECT supplier_id, avg(supplier_id).
FROM products.
Finish with GROUP BY supplier_id.
Write: SELECT supplier_id, avg(supplier_id) FROM products GROUP BY supplier_id;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT supplier_id, avg(supplier_id) FROM products GROUP BY supplier_id;
steps.memory_trick: GROUP BY = one output row per pile.

steps.title: Just the supplier_id pile (1)
steps.prompt: HAVING filters the piles after they are built - WHERE filters rows before.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT supplier_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY supplier_id HAVING supplier_id = 1;
hints: Build the piles with GROUP BY supplier_id.
Add HAVING to keep one pile.
The test is supplier_id = 1.
Write: SELECT supplier_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY supplier_id HAVING supplier_id = 1;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT supplier_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY supplier_id HAVING supplier_id = 1;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters piles.
